stateMapping.server/executions/requests/inFlight: The agent pending record of one proposal and the execute requests sent to it
stateMapping.clientProposal/consumed/attachmentDispat: AlphaClient.proposals, consumed and the approvals it dispatched for one session
stateMapping.card: The review card in the transcript: live, recovered, unavailable or done
stateMapping.reattachments: History restores and session changes that reattach the client

abstractions: One proposal identity, at most three taps and two reattachments. A history restore or session change removes the cards of the old transcript; recovery brings a pending proposal back as a recovered card.

Assumption: the agent journals each proposal identity and executes it once; a repeated execute request returns the journaled receipt. The client consumed set survives a reload of the same session, but the recovered route does not consult it, so one execution across routes rests on this assumption.
A live card whose client no longer holds the proposal sends nothing; awaiting an earlier tracked receipt on that path is omitted.
Expiry, decline, the Home review destination and read-reply completion are outside this model (see PendingActionRecovery and ReadReplyLease).

stateMapping.lease: The phase of one readReplyLeases entry
stateMapping.bindingCurrent: readReplyCurrent(binding) with the origin, digest, visibility and sensitive-screen checks
stateMapping.approval/taps: The approval in flight for the proposal
stateMapping.completions/answers/voiceResumed: completeReadReply requests, answers added to the conversation and resumeReadReplyVoice calls

abstractions: One lease. Session, conversation, origin, digest, visibility and sensitive-screen checks are one bindingCurrent predicate that never becomes true again.
A succeeded receipt stands for a receipt carrying the read-reply hint; any other receipt cancels the lease.
The answer text and message identity are omitted; the count of answers added to the conversation is tracked.

stateMapping.binding/blocked: The session, history revision and screen context the key is built from, and the conditions under which no key exists
stateMapping.read/readKey: The pendingActions request in flight and the binding it captured
stateMapping.timer/expiring: Shell.pendingActionExpiryTimer and the review cards that still carry an expiry
stateMapping.reads/triggers/applied/dropped: Requests started, the events that may start one, results applied to the cards and results ignored as stale

abstractions: Four bindings; a blocked state stands for a hidden page, a sensitive or workflow screen, connection work, a reply in progress or an approval in progress. Entering or leaving it is evaluated at once, as each of those changes updates the shell.
The pending list is reduced to how many of its review cards carry an expiry (zero to two). Which cards become recovered, unavailable or new is modeled in ApprovalRoutes.
Assumption: the agent does not return a proposal whose expiry has already passed, so an expiry read is followed by at most one further read per remaining card.
Read-reply leases retained from the pending list are modeled in ReadReplyLease.

stateMapping.phase: The review sheet, the recheck and the consume call of one question
stateMapping.current/report: options.current() and the message passed to options.report

abstractions: One notification tap and one question. Reviewability, the sensitive-text check and the excerpt are one admission class.
Home and a lost window focus are one abort action. The sheet closing after Compose is not a dismissal and changes nothing.
The sheet hands a question over only for a notification that is still current; choosing Compose for one that changed leaves the sheet open and is not a transition here.
A failed release is reported by the publisher and is outside this model; the composer that receives the draft is modeled elsewhere.

stateMapping.message/messageId/messagePlaying: The Reading state of the shell (waiting, preparing, reading, finished or failed) and its pending playback
stateMapping.note/notePlaying/noteStarted/noteOutcome: noteReading, its pending playback and the outcome readNoteAloud resolves with
stateMapping.retiring: speechRetirement and the voice conversation retirement a new reading waits for
stateMapping.starts/stops: Readings started and readings stopped before their end

abstractions: Two message identities and one note. The speech route (on-device, Cloud in pieces) is one prepare result and one playback result.
Loss of the message, screen, conversation, connection or foreground is one action. The message menu, copy and selection are outside this model.
Retirement always confirms here; a cleanup that cannot be confirmed is modeled in SpeechCleanupLatch.

stateMapping.surface/media: chatDestination and its mode, and the capture, conversation session or speech the surface holds
stateMapping.retirement: The retirement record and its phase
stateMapping.panel/restores: The chat panel state the retirement returns to
stateMapping.sendWaiting/asked/sends/staleSends/sentU: A p.send call waiting on stopVoiceConversation(): whether it went on, was dropped because the screen, conversation or draft changed while it waited, or went on although the stop was never confirmed
stateMapping.refusedStarts/holds: Refused voice starts and retirements created

abstractions: One chat shell. The surface is closed, a voice conversation or Transcribe; what it holds is one media flag.
Leaving always closes the surface. The foreground-loss path that keeps the recorder open in its ready stage, the Notes recorder and reading aloud that is stopped at entry are outside this model.
A typed message that waited on a chain that failed is sent like any other; only the later checks of p.send (empty text, a reply in progress, a held draft) are outside this model.
Whether the waiting message is still current (screen, conversation, draft, reply target) is one nondeterministic input.

stateMapping.tabs/cur/editing: renderer tab rows, the selected tab and whether its address bar is being edited (saved tabs never replace a tab being typed into)
stateMapping.created/native: native tab creation requested through the shared tab session, and the native tabs that exist
stateMapping.restored/attempts/gaveUp: cold-start tabs waiting to load their saved page, with at most two silent retries
stateMapping.nav: the one navigation in flight: creating or navigating, new tab or existing, background restore load
stateMapping.limitNotice/errorShown: the tab-limit message and a reported navigation failure

abstractions: Three tabs stand for the limit of 8 in the renderer and in the native browser. Tab identities are integers and never reused.
One navigation is in flight at a time. A second navigation started before the first settles, the approved-destination abort signal and adapter disposal are not modeled.
Native creation and page load results are nondeterministic inputs. Closing a native tab is immediate. The creation map itself is the shared tab session's.
When the selected tab closes, any remaining tab may become selected; the source picks the first remaining tab or the opener.

stateMapping.readDone/hydrated/clearing: the one saved-record read of a launch and the gate that keeps saving off until it succeeded and while data is cleared
stateMapping.content/dirty/lastSaved: the snapshot the renderer would save, input-identity change detection and the last snapshot handed to the writer
stateMapping.failed/failures/wait: a rejected write and its growing retry wait
stateMapping.inflight/pending/disk: the write the native side is handling, the one queued behind it, and the stored record
stateMapping.failed/failedContent/failures/wait: Failed content can differ from newly queued content; only the exact failed snapshot owns retry state.

abstractions: Snapshots are four content identities. The retry wait is counted in ticks (1, 2, 3) for the source's 2 s doubling to 60 s.
At most one write waits behind the write in flight; the source queue is unbounded.
The native side is taken to answer a write it received before a clear before it answers the clear.

PassedOverWriteCountsAsSavedWitness records current behavior: a queued write skipped while clearing is counted as stored, so after a failed clear the record keeps the older snapshot until another change.
Snapshot identities are ordered by inclusion: a successful read only adds saved entries to what is open, so its result is never a smaller identity.

Clear retires queued generations, drains already dispatched writes, and waits for renderer commit; failed Clear makes the unchanged snapshot retryable. Source replay drives the retained adapter saveSession directly. The separate session-saver helper is independently tested and is outside this production persistence model.

stateMapping.queue/stage/refreshQueued: the serial bookmark queue, its running operation and the one waiting refresh; an operation begins as soon as the one before it ends
stateMapping.hydrated/marks/stored: whether the list was read, the list the view shows and the saved list
stateMapping.recovery/damaged/notices/episodes: the recovery offer for a saved list that cannot be read, reported once per episode
stateMapping.disposed/marksAtDispose: a disposed adapter changes nothing it shows

abstractions: The saved list is a version number; which addresses it holds is not modeled. At most three operations wait.
A damaged list exists only on the web build, where the store refuses both reading and changing it; that refusal is an assumption about the document store, modeled in DurableStore.
UnreadWriteAttemptWitness records current behavior: once the recovery offer is shown, a bookmark change is attempted without a successful read.
The quiet first read at startup outside the Browser is not modeled.

stateMapping.finding/findTab/hasQuery/count: the find bar, the tab it belongs to and its result
stateMapping.timerArmed/timerTab/timerVersion: the 150 ms debounce before a native search
stateMapping.nativeQuery/events: tabs with an active native search and native find events not yet handled
stateMapping.alive/cur/presented: open tabs, the selected tab and the tab whose native page is shown

abstractions: Two tabs, a query that is empty or not, one result count and at most three undelivered native events. The 150 ms debounce is one nondeterministic timer.
Native find events may be delayed arbitrarily; real delivery is far faster than the debounce. Native clearing on navigation and un-presenting is the shared tab host's.

HiddenFindBarWitness and FindBarOnClosedTabWitness record current behavior: a find bar with no native search is not cleared by a tab switch or by closing its tab, and the next Back press closes it. EarlierTextSearchedWitness records that the debounce carries no query version.

stateMapping.pending/listening: open confirmation dialogs by identity and their installed listeners
stateMapping.calls/settled/last: each request settles exactly once as approved, denied or refused
stateMapping.foreground/screenLocked: app visibility and the screen lock, rechecked at the click

abstractions: Two review identities and at most three requests each. Hidden, page hide and the development background flag are one foreground flag; a screen lock arrives with its device-state event.
Dialog layout, focus return and the adapter's own confirming flag are not modeled.

stateMapping.failed/reports/recoveries: a presentation failure reported once until a success

abstractions: Two page geometries stand for all measured bounds; host rectangles, the underlay backdrop and animation-frame scheduling are not modeled.

stateMapping.unknownReceipts/unknownExists/savedRecei: Native creation journal as read by readCreations, creationPending and creationRecoveryFailed
stateMapping.selected/events: The selected device event and the provider event count
stateMapping.uncertain/uncertainKind/latchReached/lat: calendarWriteUncertain for the selected event and the forced read in refresh that releases it: the read lists the event, or covers a deleted event's start without listing it

checkCreations is modeled only while no save runs; the code has no such guard, and the check only reads and acknowledges saved receipts.

The latch is kept per event in the code; one selected event stands for it. A forced read releases the latch when it lists the event (an edit's result, or a delete the provider never applied) or when it covers a deleted event's start and no longer lists it; covers stands for the read range holding the event, and a read of another range or a failed read releases nothing.

The Android fallback from inspect to inspectDeletion is one inspection step.
A committed change to another event re-reads the rows and hands the inspected event back when its row is unchanged; the read and the hand-back are one step.
Close is taken from the rendered detail, so closeEvent needs that detail to have been rendered; a new-event form opens from the day list with no detail open.

stateMapping.saving/stage/formHasId/attemptRetained: reminderSaving, the retained creation record and the form reminderCreationId
stateMapping.opsSucceeded/opsUnknown/opStage/opRetain: Pending reminder action records and their native operation receipts
stateMapping.schedules/operates/attempts/opAttempts: scheduleReminder and operateReminder calls per handler attempt
stateMapping.formRow: The journal row of the open form's reminderCreationId: pending and not saved natively, pending and saved, or found

abstractions: Cap and OpCap of 2 stand for the 32-row creation history and the 100-row operation store; byte limits are not modeled.
Rows are counted, not identified: pending rows split into those a readback will find and those with no saved reminder.
Field-by-field matching of a saved reminder against its request is one found/not-found answer.

ownerDiscard is defined and exercised by scenarios but is not part of step: the Android reminder screens have no action that removes an unconfirmed record. The unresolvable states are reachability witnesses.
Edit, cancel, complete and snooze share one operation record shape and one flow.

The journal transitions (retain, check, retire a refused creation, reconcile, acknowledge) are the shared reminder journal; this product binds its storage and calls it from the Calendar form and event actions.
A confirmed save, a found retained form and a confirmed operation each end with a reminder refresh, which marks saved pending creations found and acknowledges operations that have a native receipt.
Creating a reminder and operating on one share reminderSaving, and a reminder detail is not reachable under an open form, so the two never run together.
lateSave names whether the reminder that turned up belongs to the open form or to an earlier creation.

stateMapping.nativeToken/issued/retained/targetListed: Native pending reminder tap, its retained target and consumption
stateMapping.interaction/interactionAt/blocked: tapInteraction fence and the eligibility gates
stateMapping.banner/detail/questionOpen: reminderTapPending, the opened reminder detail and the open question review
stateMapping.busy/requested/stage/captured/capturedQu: tapBusy, tapRequested, the awaited step of checkReminderTap and the token and question flag it read

abstractions: Up to three taps; native keeps the newest pending token, so an earlier unconsumed one is replaced.
blocked merges a hidden page, an open connection chooser, a sensitive context and an open Calendar form.
The reminder list read and the target comparison are one listed/not-listed answer; the reviewed question is consume or release.
Native token storage and its own recheck of source, occurrence and revision are modeled as "consume only the current token".

A check that ends runs a queued explicit request in the same turn; the request is dropped when the page is blocked or a question review is open, and the saved-link banner is then the only way back to the newer tap.
The question review consumes only after reading the token and the reminder again (shown page, open detail, unchanged and listed reminder); otherwise it releases.
RetainedReminderTapAdmission covers the admission after the detail render callback; this model covers the single check, its queued request and the token reads around it.

stateMapping.generation/inFlight/publishedBy/publishe: reminderRefreshGeneration and the refresh that may publish
stateMapping.deviceRows/reminderStore/shownDevice/sho: nativeCalendarRows, the reminder store, the published Calendar events and reminderStale

abstractions: Device rows and the reminder store are version numbers; up to five refreshes.
Reconciling creation and operation intents inside a refresh is covered by ReminderIntents and is part of the refresh succeeding or failing here.
A change to reminders starts a refresh in the same step (the committed and document-changed events).
The visit, view and 30-second limits on a navigation intent are covered by ReminderOpenIntent; here the intent is only opened or dropped by the newest refresh.

stateMapping.tabs.allowed: allowed(): visible, foreground, unlocked and not in mock mode
stateMapping.tabs.granted/tabs.owns/lockHolder: The alpha.browser.alarm-owner Web Lock callback, owns and release
stateMapping.tabs.ringing/tabs.sound: ringing, soundTimer and the alert audio
stateMapping.posted/versions: The set of ringing alarm rows shared by pages of one origin

abstractions: Two pages. The set of posted alarms is a version number; a changed set rings again.
allowed merges visibility, the development background flag, mock mode and the screen lock.
The one-second poll and the 60-second sound limit are nondeterministic steps; elapsed time is not counted.
This is the browser double of the Clock app. BrowserReminderOrphan covers one page against the reminder rows; the reviewed Android handoff is WorkflowClockAdmission and NativeClockReview.

stateMapping.rowsShown/rowReadDay/rowDay: Device and reminder rows whose day offset was computed when they were read
stateMapping.form/formOff/formAnchor/formIntended: Open form, its day offset and calendarDraftAnchor, calendarEditDraftAnchor or calendarPlainFormAnchor
stateMapping.saved/savedDay/savedIntended/savedWhileD: The civil day a save resolves the form offset to
stateMapping.closedEditDay: calendarEditDraftIdentity is forgotten when the editor closes, so a later editor of the same unchanged item gets a new calendarEditDraftAnchor

abstractions: Three consecutive days, one event and one form. Offsets are whole days; hours, zones and DST are not modeled.
Rows that compute their offset at each render are always current, so only device and reminder rows are modeled.
refreshDue stands for the interval between local midnight and the timer or resume that follows it. A save inside that interval, before any render, is a reachability witness.
A form no draft retains keeps a plain anchor from the first render that shows it; the model sets it when the form opens.
One form at a time: a form opens from the day list or a detail. A form replaced by another without closing, exactly across midnight, is not modeled.
Saving a device event reads the device rows again; saving a reminder form does not.

stateMapping.saved/response/outcome: Saved undated reminders as listed by the readback, the saveTodo answer and the reported result
stateMapping.listed: reminderRows as last read: the undated to-dos the view lists and can decide on

abstractions: Two texts and four ids. Title and body are one text value.
Native keeps one to-do per id and treats an identical retry as idempotent; that contract is assumed, not modeled.
Reminder form saves and reminder decisions take the same mutex and are represented by the to-do decision.
A failed readback and a readback that does not list the to-do both leave the attempt unconfirmed.
A to-do whose save is unconfirmed is saved natively and not listed until the next successful reminder read; only listed to-dos can be completed, reopened or deleted.

stateMapping.operation: the work() step in flight: Google wait, code send, resend or verification

stateMapping.incomplete/incompleteFenced/viewChanged/: queuedSignInIncomplete with its captured epoch and sign-in view, and showSignInIncomplete
stateMapping.rebindWanted/rebinds: the shared ResidentRebindQueue resumed by runQueuedResidentRebind

stateMapping.cloud/grant: Cloud delegation status and the adopted grant

Scenario and simulation evidence only; no App Link, browser or Cloud claim.

stateMapping.capability/refreshes: DeviceApps.platformCapabilities() answer and refreshImage on start and each return
